runs.text: Problem A3
Alice and Bob play a game with a string of

digits, each of which is restricted to be 0, 1, or 2. Initially all the digits are 0. A legal move is to add or subtract 1 from one digit to create a new string that has not appeared before. A player with no legal move loses, and the other player wins. Alice goes first, and the players alternate moves. For each
, determine which player has a strategy that guarantees winning.

The game is a walk through a finite graph of digit strings without revisiting a vertex. Can the second player pair most vertices so that every move into one member has an immediate move into its partner?

hints.title: Pair by the first nonzero digit

runs.text: For each nonzero string, find its first nonzero digit and change that digit from 1 to 2 or from 2 to 1. Leave every other digit fixed. Check that this operation pairs distinct strings and that paired strings differ by one legal move.

Immediately before each Alice turn, require that every pair is either completely unvisited or completely visited. If Alice enters an unvisited vertex, its partner cannot already have appeared: otherwise the invariant would say Alice's vertex had appeared too. Bob can therefore take the pairing move.

items.text: Pair all nonzero strings by flipping their first nonzero digit between 1 and 2.
Verify that the pairing is an involution and each vertex is adjacent to its partner.
After every Alice move, have Bob move to the paired vertex; prove by induction that this vertex is unused.
Use finiteness to show the game must end, and observe that Bob is never the first player without a response.
